chunks: Hisham ibn Salim said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: “I go out, and I love to be in a state of ta'qib.”
So he عليه السلام said: “If you are in a state of wudu (ablution), then you are in a state of ta'qib.”

key_terms.أَخْرُجُ: I go out; leaving one's place or departing
key_terms.مُعَقِّبًا: One engaged in ta'qib, the devotional continuation after salat (prayer)
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: Wudu (ablution), the state of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Does remaining in wudu (ablution) count as being in ta'qib after salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that remaining in a state of wudu (ablution) is sufficient for a person to be regarded as being in ta'qib. It indicates the merit of taharah (ritual purity) and its connection to the devotional state that follows salat (prayer).
